_about: How the Core assistant interprets a scheduled-maintenance milestone for the advisor: which tier each item belongs to (by PreferredTerm, or Component when there is none), what to call it to the customer, why it matters, and what skipping it risks. tiers are in the order the advisor should bring them up. recommend: true tiers are what 'Add recommended' adds. inspectionGroups names the systems the bundled multi-point inspection covers, by keyword in the check's name. Wording is customer-facing: plain, no pressure, no claims beyond the schedule.

tiers.label: Safety
tiers.say: These affect how the vehicle stops, steers and grips the road.

tiers.label: Protects the engine
tiers.say: These help keep the engine and drivetrain from wearing early, per the manufacturer's schedule.

tiers.label: Comfort and efficiency
tiers.say: These are part of the schedule but can wait if the customer would rather keep today's bill down.

engine oil.why: Fresh oil helps protect the engine's moving parts.
engine oil.skip: Oil breaks down over time, and old oil can lead to sludge and added engine wear.

engine oil filter.why: Fresh oil helps protect the engine's moving parts.
engine oil filter.skip: Oil breaks down over time, and old oil can lead to sludge and added engine wear.

spark plug.why: Worn plugs can cause misfires, rough running and lower fuel economy.
spark plug.skip: Over time, misfires can damage other parts such as the catalytic converter.

engine coolant.why: Coolant protection wears out over time.
engine coolant.skip: Old coolant can allow corrosion in the cooling system.

transmission fluid.why: Fresh fluid helps the transmission shift smoothly and run cool.
transmission fluid.skip: Worn fluid can add wear to the transmission.

differential fluid.why: It lubricates the gears that drive the wheels.
differential fluid.skip: Worn fluid can add wear to the gears.

transfer case fluid.skip: Worn fluid can add wear to the all-wheel-drive system.

drive belt.why: The belt drives the alternator, A/C and water pump.
drive belt.skip: A worn belt can crack or break, which can affect those systems.

vacuum pump.why: It supplies power assist for the brakes on this engine.
vacuum pump.skip: A failing pump can make the brake pedal harder to press.

battery.why: A weak battery is a common cause of no-start problems.
battery.skip: Batteries tend to weaken with age, especially in cold weather.

high voltage battery air filter.why: It helps keep the hybrid battery cool.
high voltage battery air filter.skip: A clogged filter can make the hybrid battery run warmer.

FUEL ADDITIVE.why: It helps keep the fuel injectors clean.
FUEL ADDITIVE.skip: Deposits can build up over time and affect fuel economy.

tires.why: Rotating helps the tires wear evenly and last longer.
tires.skip: Uneven wear can shorten tire life and affect handling.

disc brake pad.skip: Pads worn past their limit can damage the rotors and affect braking.

brake system.why: An inspection can find worn parts early.
brake system.skip: Brake wear left unchecked can lead to a larger repair.

window wiper blade.why: Good blades help keep the windshield clear in rain.
window wiper blade.skip: Worn blades can streak and reduce visibility.

cabin air filter.why: It filters the air coming through the vents and helps the A/C airflow.
cabin air filter.skip: A clogged filter can reduce airflow and cause odors.

engine air filter.why: A clean filter helps fuel economy and performance.
engine air filter.skip: A dirty filter can gradually reduce fuel economy.

fuel cap seal.why: A worn seal can turn on the check engine light.
fuel cap seal.skip: A worn seal can set off the check engine light.
